key_insight: Plaquette links real hardware noise models directly to fault-tolerant logical performance, going beyond Pauli-only approximations to capture leakage, coherent errors, and non-Markovian device physics.
engineering_relevance: It helps quantum hardware teams choose which imperfections matter most and estimate thresholds, overheads, and error budgets using simulation matched to the platform’s actual noise.
method: Supports Kraus-operator, Hamiltonian-Lindblad, or reconstructed-channel inputs.
Automatically compiles one noise model into multiple samplers: stabilizer, XPauli, near-Clifford, or full-state.
Targets platform-specific errors such as transmon leakage, neutral-atom scattering, and ion-trap heating.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that XPauli and near-Clifford samplers match full-state simulation within statistical uncertainty, while Pauli twirling can deviate depending on the error model.
watch_item: Accurate results depend on choosing and validating the right hardware noise representation, since simplified Clifford-only or twirled models can misestimate performance for some devices.
paper_title: Plaquette: A hardware-aware design platform for fault-tolerant quantum computers
